implementation_statement: Access control policy POL-02 (2023) was revised and approved 2026-09-15, effective 2026-10-01 (P06). It now covers OT components and shared accounts. The CTC field access procedure and the shared account standard (STD-06) are in draft.

Directory and identity provider accounts are provisioned from the HR feed; terminations disable directory and IdP access automatically. IT accounts are reviewed quarterly. Gaps: CAD/CTC, BOS, and TMS application roles are reviewed only annually; 2 shared dispatcher logins remain at the backup NOC; crew tablet accounts disabled up to 5 days late (gap 9); 3 shared maintainer accounts per CTC field platform unchanged since 2023 (gap 2).
evidence: IdP and directory exports; quarterly IT review records; CAD/CTC user list 2026-07; P07 samples

implementation_statement: Access to CAD/CTC functions is enforced by application roles (dispatcher, chief dispatcher, supervisor, maintainer, read-only). BOS administration is limited to the PTC administrator role. Directory groups control file and server access.
evidence: CAD/CTC role matrix; BOS role export

implementation_statement: Deny-by-default rules on the IT/OT boundary firewalls at the HQ data center and both NOCs allow only documented flows (TMS consist feed, crew system lookup, backup jobs, PAM jump host sessions, time and patch services). Gap: inside the field backhaul, the CTC code line, radio, detector, and crossing monitor traffic share one flat network with no flow control between them (gap 1).
evidence: Firewall rule export; flow inventory 2026-07; field network diagram (2022)

implementation_statement: Dispatcher and maintainer roles are separated in the CAD/CTC system. Signal maintainers cannot issue movement authority. Gap: 2 CTC maintenance workstation users also hold CAD/CTC administrator rights.
evidence: CAD/CTC role matrix; P07 AC-6 test

implementation_statement: Least privilege is enforced for IT servers and cloud through the PAM tool with just-in-time elevation. Gaps: CAD/CTC administrator rights held by 2 maintainers (AC-5); field controller shared maintainer accounts give every maintainer full configuration rights.
evidence: PAM policy export; CAD/CTC admin list

implementation_statement: Security functions (firewall rules, EDR policy, PAM vaults, OT sensor configuration) are limited to the 7-person cybersecurity team and 2 network engineers.
Administrators use separate privileged accounts, checked out through the PAM tool, for IT servers, the CAD/CTC servers, the BOS, and cloud consoles. Daily-use accounts have no administrator rights.
Privileged accounts are restricted to 64 named accounts across IT, cloud, CAD/CTC, and BOS. Cloud root credentials are sealed with hardware MFA; break-glass accounts are stored offline at each NOC.
PAM sessions are recorded and logged to the SIEM. Gap: privileged actions inside the CAD/CTC application and on the BOS are logged locally only (gap 7).
evidence: PAM session logs; SIEM source list

implementation_statement: Directory and IdP lock accounts after 10 failed attempts for 15 minutes. CAD/CTC consoles lock after 5 failed attempts and alert the chief dispatcher; unlock by the help desk after identity check.

Office endpoints lock after 15 minutes. Dispatch consoles do not auto-lock (safety requirement for continuous display); compensating controls: badge-controlled NOC, consoles in view of the chief dispatcher, and per-dispatcher logins at handover.
evidence: Group policy export; NOC access list

implementation_statement: Staff remote access uses the company VPN with MFA. CAD/CTC and PTC vendors reach the TDPO only through the PAM jump host with MFA, approval per session, and recording. Gap: the radio system vendor (site-to-site VPN) and the detector vendor (cellular modems) have always-on access outside the jump host (gap 3).
evidence: VPN and PAM configuration; vendor access list

implementation_statement: Jump host sessions are monitored and recorded, and the MSSP alerts on sessions outside approved windows. The radio and detector vendor paths are not monitored.
evidence: PAM session report; MSSP use case list

control_name: Protection of Confidentiality and Integrity Using Encryption
implementation_statement: Remote access sessions use the company VPN (IPsec) or TLS to the jump host; vendor paths through the jump host are encrypted end to end.

Office Wi-Fi uses enterprise authentication and is separated from the dispatch zones. Radio data links for the code line use the vendor's link encryption. Gap: 6 tower sites still use legacy unencrypted links for detector alarms.

The 410 crew tablets are enrolled in mobile device management: passcode, encryption, remote wipe, approved apps only. Tablets reach the bulletin and train list services through an app gateway, not the dispatch zone.
POL-05 prohibits use of personal devices and external systems to process TDPO data except the approved crew tablet apps; vendor laptops may not connect to dispatch zones.
Security awareness and training policy and procedures are part of POL-01 and POL-05 (approved 2026-09-15) and the TSA-approved security training program.
evidence: POL-05; TSA training program approval letter

implementation_statement: All employees complete annual security awareness training; office users receive quarterly phishing simulations (June 2026 click rate 5.1%). Security-sensitive employees also receive the TSA-approved security training (1580.115), with recurrent training every 3 years.
evidence: Training completion report (96%); phishing report; TSA training records

implementation_statement: Dispatchers, chief dispatchers, PTC administrators, and signal maintainers receive role training on their systems. Gap: no cybersecurity content in dispatcher or maintainer training (recognizing and reporting a cyber event, manual dispatch on a cyber trigger, OT isolation steps).
Training records (name, job function, date of hire, dates, course, length, topics) are kept for 5 years in the learning system, as 1570.121(a) requires for TSA security training.
Logging requirements sit in POL-03 and the draft logging and monitoring standard STD-02 (due 2027-01-31).

Event types are defined for directory, IdP, firewalls, VPN, PAM, EDR, cloud control plane, and Windows servers and consoles. Gap: CAD/CTC application events (logons, authority changes, administrator actions), BOS events, and field controller events are not defined or collected (gap 7).

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: The MSSP reviews and correlates IT logs 24x7 and escalates high-severity alerts within 30 minutes. OT sensor alerts at the NOCs are reviewed weekly by the OT security engineer, not in real time. CAD/CTC and BOS logs are reviewed only during investigations.
evidence: MSSP monthly reports; OT sensor review log

implementation_statement: Servers, consoles, firewalls, and the BOS synchronize to the company time servers, which use GPS-disciplined sources at both NOCs.
Logs forwarded to the SIEM and the write-once log bucket in the shared services account cannot be changed by system administrators.
SIEM keeps 1 year searchable; the log bucket keeps 3 years. Gap: CAD/CTC, BOS, and field device logs overwrite locally after about 30 days, too short for investigations (SD III.D.3.b).
Log generation is enabled on IT systems and the dispatch consoles. CAD/CTC and BOS generate application logs that are not forwarded; field controllers generate minimal logs.
Assessment and authorization policy is in POL-01 (statements on independent annual assessment and the TSA Cybersecurity Assessment Plan).

The TSA-approved Cybersecurity Assessment Plan (most recent approval 2025-06-20) schedules assessments of CIP measures. Gap: the 2025-26 annual report (2026-06-18) showed 29% of CIP measures assessed, below the one-third minimum (gap 5). The 2026 P07 assessment by the co-sourced internal audit firm covers 34 controls and brings the current plan year to 41%.

Interconnection terms exist with the host Class I (PTC interoperability agreement), the 2 Class I interchange partners (EDI agreements), and the TMS vendor (contract). Gap: the services agreements with the affiliates do not describe the interconnection or security responsibilities.
evidence: Interoperability agreement; EDI agreements; services agreements

implementation_statement: A POA&M is kept in the GRC tool, reviewed monthly by the Cybersecurity Manager and quarterly by the COO and the audit committee (P07 `poam.csv`).

Continuous monitoring covers IT through the MSSP and the dispatch zones through the OT sensors. Gap: no monitoring of field zones; monthly metrics do not yet include OT patch age or inventory completeness.

baseline: Added by tailoring (not in Moderate baseline)
implementation_statement: Selected by tailoring (not in the Moderate baseline) because SD III.F.2.c calls for penetration testing. Annual external and internal penetration tests of IT since 2024 (last 2026-04). Gap: no adversarial testing of the OT zones or the PTC back office; a purple team exercise on the TDPO is planned for 2027 Q1.

Internal connections between the dispatch zones, the BOS, and the field backhaul are listed in the CIP. Gap: the field network diagrams date from 2022, and 9 tower-site connections found in P07 were not on them.
Configuration management policy sits in POL-01 and POL-04; the configuration standard STD-01 (IT and OT baselines) is in draft, due 2027-03-31.

Baseline configurations exist for Windows servers and consoles (benchmark-based) and for the IT/OT boundary firewalls. Gap: no documented baselines for field communication controllers, radio gateways, or detector modems.

Changes to CAD/CTC and the BOS go through the change advisory board with vendor certification and a rollback plan. Gap: field controller configuration changes are made by maintainers without a change ticket; 6 of 20 sampled field changes had no record.
Impact analysis is required for CAD/CTC and BOS changes, including operational testing on the vendor's test system. Not required for field controller firmware changes.
Only change-approved administrators, through the PAM tool, can change CAD/CTC and BOS servers; field equipment housings are locked (236.3).
Benchmark settings are applied to Windows servers and consoles by group policy; 8 of 10 sampled servers met the benchmark in P07. CAD/CTC servers have 11 vendor-required deviations, documented.
Dispatch consoles run an application allowlist; unused services are disabled on CAD/CTC and BOS servers per the vendor hardening guides.

IT assets are inventoried automatically (EDR and MDM). The OT inventory (CIP Critical Cyber Systems) is about 70% complete: tower sites, crossing monitors, and detector modems lack firmware versions (gap 8).
evidence: Asset inventory export; OT sensor asset list

implementation_statement: Users cannot install software on consoles or office endpoints; installs go through the software center or change control.
Contingency planning policy sits in POL-03; the contingency and recovery standard STD-07 is in draft, due 2026-12-31.

The TDPO contingency plan (2025) covers failover to the backup NOC and standby servers. Gaps: it does not cover recovery from backups after a cyber event, manual dispatch in CTC territory, or the order for isolating OT (gap 6). The BIA (P05) now supplies the recovery objectives.
Dispatchers practice failover to the backup NOC twice a year. Manual dispatch training covers track warrant territory only.

Backup NOC failover was tested 2026-03 (passed). Gaps: no end-to-end restore of CAD/CTC or BOS from the write-once backups; no manual dispatch drill in CTC territory (gap 6). First restore test scheduled 2026-11-05.
Backups of CAD/CTC, BOS, and the crew system go to the separate backup account in a second cloud region, with separate administrator credentials.
The backup NOC at Jacksonville Terminal Yard (6 consoles, standby CAD/CTC and BOS) is the alternate processing site, about 150 miles from HQ.
The code line uses company radio and microwave with 2 leased circuits; the NOCs have diverse carriers. Gap: one leased circuit is a single path for 11 control points.

Daily backups of CAD/CTC and BOS databases and weekly system images go to the backup account with 35-day write-once retention; backups are scanned with EDR at backup time (SD 1580-21-01E II.D.1.b). Field controller configurations are archived after each change.
evidence: Backup job reports (30 of 30 days in July); scan logs

implementation_statement: Rebuild procedures exist for consoles and Windows servers. Gap: no tested procedure to rebuild CAD/CTC or the BOS from backups into a clean environment; the RTO of 2 hours is not demonstrated (P05 finding 1).
Identification and authentication policy is in POL-02 (approved 2026-09-15), including memorized secret reset criteria aligned with NIST SP 800-63.
Unique accounts are required for all users of IT systems, CAD/CTC, and the BOS. Gaps: 2 shared dispatcher logins at the backup NOC; shared maintainer accounts on field controllers (gap 2).
MFA is required for all privileged access through the PAM tool and for cloud administration. CAD/CTC and BOS administration is reached only through the PAM tool, so MFA applies.
evidence: PAM and IdP policies; P07 MFA test

implementation_statement: MFA is required for email, VPN, TMS, and cloud. Dispatch consoles do not use MFA; compensating controls are documented in the CIP (badge-controlled NOC, console zone isolation, per-dispatcher logins). Gap: the backup NOC shared logins defeat the compensating control.
The BOS authenticates onboard units and the host's PTC components with certificates. Field controllers authenticate to the CAD/CTC front end by address only.
Identifiers are assigned from HR records and never reused; vendor identifiers are named and tied to a sponsor.

Password policy follows POL-02 (14 characters, banned list, reset on evidence of compromise). Gaps: field controller shared passwords unchanged since 2023; default vendor passwords on detector modems and crossing monitors (gap 2).
evidence: Password policy; P07 default credential test

implementation_statement: Incident response policy POL-03 (approved 2026-09-15) sets roles, TSA and CISA reporting, and evidence handling.
The incident response team trains annually. Gap: chief dispatchers and signal supervisors, who must execute isolation and manual dispatch, have not been trained on the plan (SD 1580-21-01E II.D.3.b).

The Cybersecurity Incident Response Plan is exercised annually (2025-10 tabletop tested containment and backup integrity objectives). Gap: the IT/OT isolation objective (II.D.1.c) has never been exercised, and operations staff did not take part (gap 6).

Incident handling follows POL-03 and the P08 runbooks: MSSP triage, company incident commander, outside counsel and forensics through the insurer. Gap: OT containment steps rely on undocumented knowledge of 2 engineers.
Incidents are tracked in the incident log with discovery time, classification, and reporting decisions.

POL-03 and P08 set the reporting chain: TSA TSOC call within 12 hours (company target; IC Surface-2025-01 recommendation), CISA report within 72 hours stating it is made under the directive (SD 1580-21-01E II.C), and the 1570.203 duty met through that report. Gap: the report template lacked the required statement and the incident content list until 2026-09.
evidence: Report template v2; P08 notification matrix

provider_if_inherited: MSSP; forensic firm through insurer panel
implementation_statement: MSSP incident response hours and the insurer's panel forensic firm are on retainer; CISA and the TSA Surface Operations contacts are listed in the binder.
The Cybersecurity Incident Response Plan (2025-04) names positions and resources (SD II.D.2). Gaps: it lacks the TMS vendor outage scenario and the OT isolation decision order; P08 adds both.
Maintenance of CAD/CTC and BOS servers is scheduled through change control; field equipment maintenance follows the signal maintenance program.

Nonlocal maintenance by the CAD/CTC and PTC vendors runs through the PAM jump host with MFA, per-session approval, and recording. Gap: radio and detector vendors maintain equipment through always-on paths (gap 3).
evidence: PAM session records; vendor access list

responsible_role: Director of Safety, Security, and Hazmat
implementation_statement: SSI is marked under 49 CFR 1520.13 on CIP, CAP, and TSA correspondence. Gap: CAP annual report drafts were unmarked (gap 11).

responsible_role: Director of Safety, Security, and Hazmat
implementation_statement: SSI is stored in a restricted document library with need-to-know groups. Gap: 4 copies of CIP sections were found in 2 broader file shares (gap 11).
Server and console drives are wiped to NIST SP 800-88 or destroyed with certificates; returned locomotive PTC hardware is wiped by the PTC vendor.

responsible_role: Director of Safety, Security, and Hazmat
implementation_statement: Access to both NOCs and the data centers is authorized by the Director of Network Operations or Director of IT; lists reviewed quarterly.

responsible_role: Director of Safety, Security, and Hazmat
implementation_statement: Badge access and CCTV at both NOCs and the HQ data center. Signal housings and tower shelters are locked (236.3). Gap: tower shelters use 3 common keys held by about 90 people; key logs are incomplete.
This SSP (P02) is the first for the TDPO. The CIP describes the same systems for TSA; this SSP is cross-referenced to it and will be maintained annually.
Rules of behavior (POL-05) are acknowledged at hire and annually; NOC-specific rules cover consoles, radios, and phones.

The CIP defense-in-depth design (zones, boundaries, jump host) is the security architecture. Gap: field zones are not yet designed in detail (gap 1); the architecture design review is overdue (gap 5).

baseline: Added by tailoring (not in Moderate baseline)
implementation_statement: Selected by tailoring (program management). The program plan is POL-01 plus the CIP, CAP, and this SSP.

baseline: Added by tailoring (not in Moderate baseline)
implementation_statement: Selected by tailoring. The Cybersecurity Manager is the primary TSA Cybersecurity Coordinator and the Director of IT the alternate, both U.S. citizens, reported to TSA within 7 days of changes (SD 1580-21-01E II.B).

baseline: Added by tailoring (not in Moderate baseline)
implementation_statement: Selected by tailoring. Risk appetite and acceptance authorities are set in POL-01 and the risk register (P01), approved by the CEO 2026-09-15.

baseline: Added by tailoring (not in Moderate baseline)
implementation_statement: Selected by tailoring. Threat information comes from TSA, CISA, the rail industry information sharing center, and the MSSP; the Cybersecurity Coordinator distributes advisories.
Background checks are done at hire for all employees; dispatchers and IT staff also get criminal history checks.
Terminations disable directory and IdP access the same day. Gaps: crew tablet and TMS accounts up to 5 days late; shared field passwords not changed (gap 2, gap 9).
Transfers trigger a role review in the IdP. Gap: CAD/CTC roles are not reviewed on transfer.
Vendor staff with TDPO access are named, sponsored, and use jump host accounts. Gap: no security clauses with radio and detector vendors (gap 10).
The TDPO is categorized Moderate (section 6 of this SSP).
Annual risk assessment per SP 800-30 (P01, 2026-07-31), covering IT and OT.

Monthly authenticated scans of IT and the dispatch consoles; passive OT asset and vulnerability identification at the NOCs. Gap: no vulnerability data for field devices; KEV entries on 2 controller firmware versions found only in P07.
Critical Cyber Systems are identified in the CIP and confirmed by the BIA (P05).
New contracts for TDPO components include security terms (patch support, vulnerability notice, remote access rules). Gap: legacy OT vendor contracts do not (gap 10).
External services (TMS, PTC managed service, MSSP, cloud) are reviewed annually through SOC 2 reports (P09). Gap: MSSP contract excludes OT; TMS RTO does not meet the BIA.
CAD/CTC runs on a supported OS version. Gap: 18 crossing monitors and 4 detector modems are past vendor support; replacement is in the 2027 capital plan.
IT/OT boundary firewalls at the HQ data center and both NOCs deny by default. Gap: no boundaries inside the field backhaul (gap 1); field zone design due 2027-03-31.

control_name: Deny by Default, Allow by Exception
implementation_statement: Boundary firewalls deny all traffic except documented flows (Deny by Default, Allow by Exception).

provider_if_inherited: Industry interoperable messaging network; host Class I
implementation_statement: PTC messages use the message integrity and authentication the host's certified system requires (236.1033). TMS feeds use TLS. Gap: code line traffic between field controllers and the front end is not encrypted on 2 leased circuits; compensating control is the vital field logic.
PTC keys are managed under the host railroad's key management process; company TLS certificates are issued from the internal CA with 1-year life.
PTC message authentication uses the algorithms specified by the host's certified system; TLS 1.2 or higher elsewhere.
CAD/CTC and BOS databases and backups are encrypted at rest; cloud volumes and backups use company-managed keys.

IT systems are patched monthly; KEV items within 14 days. Gaps: CAD/CTC servers 14 months behind vendor-certified patches; 2 controller firmware versions with KEV entries and no documented mitigations or timeline (gap 4).
EDR runs on all Windows servers and consoles (vendor-certified for CAD/CTC since 2025) with MSSP response.
MSSP monitors IT 24x7; OT sensors watch NOC and data center traffic against a baseline. Gap: no monitoring of field zones or of OT external connections outside the NOCs (SD III.D.2.b).
evidence: Monitoring use cases; OT sensor coverage map

implementation_statement: TSA, CISA, and vendor advisories are received by the Cybersecurity Coordinators and tracked to closure.
CAD/CTC and BOS software packages are hash-verified against vendor releases before install. Field controller firmware is not verified.
The BOS validates consist data from the TMS (car counts, tonnage, length, hazmat positions) before PTC initialization and rejects mismatches.

responsible_role: Director of Safety, Security, and Hazmat
implementation_statement: Train sheets, warrants, and the dispatcher log are kept 3 years; chain-of-custody records 60 days or longer (1580.205(h)); TSA training records 5 years.
Supply chain risk is addressed in the draft vendor risk standard STD-03; no separate plan yet.
OT component purchases need Signals and Communications and cybersecurity approval. Gap: no requirement for vendor vulnerability disclosure or firmware signing.
Tier 1 vendors are reviewed annually (P09). Gap: 4 OT vendors have never been assessed.
